clue.text: Instrumentalists' money-belt?

definitions.note: the definition is a possessive plural noun, while the answer names the group of players itself

parts.note: brass is British slang for money
a band is a strip or belt of material

explanation.surface: A query about the belt in which some musicians keep their cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is only loosely attached: a group of instrumentalists playing trumpets, cornets and tubas.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of musicians playing horns and tubas together is the classic ensemble of that kind.

clue.text: Share of the gardening profits?

parts.note: a cut taken from earnings, read as though it came from the garden tool used on leaves

explanation.surface: A gardener asks about their cut of the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: The slang for an illicit cut of profits sounds like work done with a garden tool, hence 'gardening'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a commission or illegal cut skimmed from takings.

clue.text: Second team to go down

parts.note: a sub is a second-in-command, a subordinate or substitute
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: The reserve team facing relegation.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink or settle lower, as floodwater or a fever does.

clue.text: Gambler almost about to do an errand for a young lady

indicators.note: about means going round, so the trimmed gambler surrounds the errand
almost the whole word, so the final letter of the gambler is dropped

parts.note: a better is one who bets
to run an errand is to go and do it

explanation.surface: A gambler sends a young woman out on an errand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the gambler's last letter, and 'about' wraps what remains around the errand; 'Gambler' reads as the definition at first, but the young lady comes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark-haired woman or girl; the answer specifically describes hair colour.

clue.text: Girl had pen removed

indicators.note: removed suggests letters shifted from their places, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl's pen was taken from her.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name from Greek myth, the nymph turned into a laurel.

clue.text: Neutral county?

parts.note: neutral read as neither male nor female, i.e. between the two genders, gives the name of an old English county

explanation.surface: Which English county stays neutral?
explanation.walkthrough: An old county bordering London; 'neutral' is read as the sex in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A former English county around north-west London whose name splits as a sex in the middle.

clue.text: Article linking two vehicles to make a third

indicators.note: linking says the article sits between and joins the two vehicles

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a van is another vehicle
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece about a coupling of car and trailer making another kind of transport.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is itself a third vehicle, a towed home on wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A towed mobile home is a third vehicle beside the motor car and the van.

clue.text: A legal right a boy transferred

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy hands over a legal claim.
explanation.walkthrough: In law, to alienate property is to transfer its ownership.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal sense: property conveyed to another owner has been handed over.

clue.text: A large drink said to be for a girl

parts.note: big means large

indicators.note: said marks a word heard spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: Someone orders a big drink for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, also an old word for a lady's maid.

clue.text: Heavenly colour?

parts.note: heavenly read literally as of the firmament overhead, giving that pale shade

explanation.surface: Asking what colour heaven is.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale bright shade like a clear daytime firmament.

clue.text: Form of dry heat used to produce a chemical compound

indicators.note: a form of the words means their letters shaped anew

explanation.surface: Applying dry heat to make a chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: A compound in which water molecules are bound in with another substance.

clue.text: One is in force to maintain the law

definitions.text: One is in force to maintain the law

parts.words: One is in force to maintain the law
parts.note: a member of the force, i.e. a constabulary, whose job is upholding the law

explanation.surface: A statement about someone who keeps law and order.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer of the constabulary enforces law and order.

clue.text: A step up?

definitions.note: up as in mounted on a horse, the definition being an adverb

parts.note: a stride is a long step

explanation.surface: Asking whether a step goes upward.
explanation.walkthrough: A jockey who is 'up' sits with legs either side of the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with legs on either side, like a rider in the saddle.

clue.text: An Easter rendering of a pastoral cantata

indicators.note: a rendering is a version, so the letters are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A performance of a cantata at Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: An eighteenth-century dramatic cantata, often on a pastoral theme.

clue.text: Pretend to touch the feelings of another

definitions.meaning: to put on, feign or assume

definitions.text: to touch the feelings of another

explanation.definitionFit: One verb means to feign a manner and also to move someone emotionally.

clue.text: An ill-equipped vehicle

parts.note: ill-equipped read not as badly fitted out but as fitted out for the ill

explanation.surface: A complaint about a poorly kitted-out vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle carrying sick or injured people, equipped for them.

clue.text: Pork received with a poor reception

definitions.meaning: the crisp roasted skin of a pork joint
crackle and hiss on a radio with bad signal

explanation.definitionFit: Crisp roast pig skin, and the hissing noise of a weak radio signal.

clue.text: Salesman to get up and resume action

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to rise is to get up

explanation.surface: A salesman gets up and goes back to work.
explanation.walkthrough: In music or theatre, to repeat or take up again a piece or role.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up or repeat again, as a role or a musical theme.

clue.text: Spanish lady, one's turned to an English one

definitions.text: Spanish lady, one's turned to an English one

parts.words: Spanish lady, one's turned to an English one
parts.note: a young Spanish woman's title which, translated, becomes the English title Miss

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman is converted into an Englishwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' here means translated: the Spanish title for an unmarried young woman becomes Miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A young unmarried woman in Spain, addressed by the equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: Many recorded that it had become blocked

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, a crossword many
logged means written down in a record

explanation.surface: Lots of people recorded that something got blocked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopped up or obstructed, like a drain full of debris.

clue.text: Left divorcee a change of diet

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: a change means the word diet has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A divorced woman left and changed her diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a political label or a direction, but it is the past tense of leave; 'a change of' scrambles the diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Went out of a place, departed.

clue.text: Come into money without earning it

definitions.text: Come into money without earning it

parts.words: Come into money without earning it
parts.note: to receive wealth through someone's will rather than by work

explanation.surface: Getting rich with no effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To receive property or money from someone who has died.

clue.text: Involve one in hostility with another to bring affairs into confusion

definitions.text: Involve one in hostility with another
definitions.meaning: to drag someone into a quarrel

explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers dragging someone into a conflict and throwing matters into turmoil.

clue.text: Bald?

parts.note: hairless read as having no locks of hair, i.e. not secured with locks

explanation.surface: A one-word query about hairlessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a pun: without locks of hair, like a door left open.

clue.text: Leave out old establishment point

parts.note: ex means former or old
CE stands for the Church of England, the established church

explanation.surface: A former establishment's point is ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church of England is the 'Establishment' church, abbreviated CE.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to exclude or omit from a list.

clue.text: One who dislikes foreigners will vandalise phone-boxes endlessly

indicators.note: vandalise means smash up, so the letters are wrecked into a new order
endlessly takes off the last letter of the boxes

explanation.surface: A bigot who smashes up telephone kiosks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the S off PHONEBOXES; 'will vandalise' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with an irrational fear or hatred of people from other countries.

clue.text: Heavenly messenger in charge

parts.note: an angel is a messenger of God

explanation.surface: A messenger from heaven running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly messenger' looks like one unit, but 'Heavenly' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Of or like the beings of paradise; saintly, divine.

clue.text: Pantomime character causes the jetty to collapse?

parts.note: a pier is a jetty
rot means decay or collapse

explanation.surface: A clown's antics bring down the pier.
explanation.walkthrough: PIERROT is the sad white-faced clown of French pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: The white-faced sad clown of French pantomime and commedia.

clue.text: Make a profit from the elimination of crime

definitions.meaning: a ... campaign rids an area of crime

explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb for raking in big gains, and a noun for a sweep ridding an area of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Soldier hurried with you in France to Los Angeles on seeing a hairy horror

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
ran means hurried
tu is French for you

explanation.surface: A soldier rushes with a French friend to California and meets a big spider.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hairy spider, a frightening creature to many.
